title: Pan Dulce with Fruit, No Frosting

content.title: About
content.content: Pan Dulce is a traditional Mexican sweet bread made from a soft, yeasted dough. This version incorporates fresh fruit pieces (such as strawberry, kiwi or mango) and omits any frosting, resulting in a lighter, less sweet treat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pan Dulce originated in Mexico in the 19th century and quickly became a holiday staple.
Traditional recipes often include cinnamon, vanilla and orange zest, but this variant focuses on a fruit filling.
Fruit versions are frequently served chilled to preserve the freshness and aroma of the berries.
Skipping the frosting makes the product more suitable for those watching sugar intake.
The dough is made with flour, eggs, butter and milk, giving it a tender crumb.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: The fresh fruit adds vitamin C, vitamin A and folate, which support immune function.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fruit and whole‑grain flour contribute dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Without frosting, the amount of added simple sugars is reduced, beneficial for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Butter provides monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Carbohydrates from flour and fruit deliver quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Standard flour contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Certain fruits may cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Natural fruit sugars
items.content: Even without frosting, fruits contain natural sugars, which should be considered by diabetics.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Butter and eggs make the product calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pan Dulce with fruit can be enjoyed as a standalone dessert, sliced into bite‑size pieces and paired with yogurt, ice cream or fresh juice. It also makes a convenient on‑the‑go snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer shelf life keep refrigerated for up to 5 days or freeze wrapped tightly in plastic.
